authoringNote: Ten original Year 6 writing prompts, two for each of narrative, persuasive, descriptive, informative and expository writing, each sized for a 15-minute response. Unsigned AI drafts: no independent originality review, human approval or publication is claimed. They are not reachable by any learner route.

prompts.title: The note on the last page
prompts.prompt:
While tidying a shelf in the school library, you open an old book and find that its last page has been taken out and replaced with a handwritten note. The note has your name on it.

Write a story about what the note says and what you decide to do next.

prompts.title: When the lighthouse went dark
prompts.prompt:
For a hundred years the lighthouse at the end of Mariner's Point has shone every night. Tonight, as a storm rolls in, its light suddenly goes out.

Write a story about what happens next, told by someone who lives nearby.

prompts.title: A garden in the car park
prompts.prompt:
Your school council is deciding whether to turn an unused corner of the car park into a vegetable garden looked after by students.

Write a persuasive piece for the school newsletter. Argue either for or against the plan, and give reasons that would convince a parent reading it.

prompts.title: The pool or the skate park
prompts.prompt:
A small town can afford only one of two projects: repairing its old public swimming pool, or building a new skate park beside the river.

Write a letter to the mayor persuading them to choose one project over the other. Use reasons and examples to support your choice.

prompts.title: The market at lighting-up time
prompts.prompt:
Describe an outdoor market at the moment the stalls are being lit for the evening.

Use what can be seen, heard, smelt, tasted and felt so that your reader feels as though they are walking between the stalls.

prompts.title: Rain after the dry
prompts.prompt:
After a long, dry summer, the first rain finally reaches a farm. Describe the moments when the rain arrives, as seen, heard and smelt by someone standing on the verandah.

Choose your words carefully so the reader can picture it.

prompts.title: A guide for a new student
prompts.prompt:
A younger student is about to join your school next term and is nervous about the first week.

Write an information guide that helps them settle in. Organise it so they can find things easily, and include the facts and tips you think matter most.

prompts.title: A job in our community
prompts.prompt:
Choose one job that helps your community, such as a nurse, a bus driver, a baker or a council gardener.

Write an information report that explains what the person does, what skills the job needs and why the work matters to the people around them.

prompts.title: Starting is easier than finishing
prompts.prompt:
Many people find it easier to begin something new than to see it through to the end.

Write an explanation of why you think this happens, and discuss what can help a person keep going. Use examples to make your ideas clear.

prompts.title: A friend who tells the truth
prompts.prompt:
Someone once said, "A good friend is someone who tells you the truth."

Write an essay explaining what you think this means. Discuss whether it is always true, and use examples from real life or from stories you know.
